title: Match Messaging Engagement Metric Critique
scenario: BooedUp wants to measure messaging engagement after users establish a Match connection. The team believes stronger messaging engagement leads to offline dates and long-term retention.
prompt: A product manager proposes tracking 'Total messages sent by Matched users' as the primary messaging engagement metric. The team will report this number weekly to leadership and use it to evaluate experiments that aim to increase conversation depth. What is wrong with this metric? Propose a corrected version.
instructions: One short sentence: name the flaw, propose a fix. Example format: 'Should be normalized. [Corrected Metric Name] is better.'
stakeholder_rationale: Total messages shows whether Matches are actually talking after connecting.
expected_themes: messages per Match is the right denominator
reference_answer: Should be normalized per Match. Messages per Match connection is better.

grading_rubric.criterion: Identifies lack of normalization as the flaw
grading_rubric.description: Answer explicitly states the metric is not normalized, is a raw count, or does not account for varying Match volumes

grading_rubric.criterion: Proposes a rate metric with Match connections as denominator
grading_rubric.description: Corrected metric divides messages by Match connections (or active Matches, or new Matches in period)
Answer follows 'flaw + corrected metric' format in one concise sentence

hints: Think about whether this metric allows fair comparison across weeks with different Match volumes.
Consider what happens if Match connections double but engagement per Match stays flat.
A normalized metric would divide by the number of Match connections in the period.
common_mistakes: Proposing 'messages per user' instead of 'messages per Match' — misses that not all users have Matches
Suggesting median instead of mean without recognizing the core flaw is lack of normalization
Critiquing the metric as a 'vanity metric' without naming the specific structural flaw
Proposing a complex segmentation instead of a simple per-Match rate
